nodes.title: 💡Video Generation Tips
widgets_values:
**The Stage 1 video is completely optional!** You can bypass this group to skip the process and save time. However, keep in mind that the optional color correction in Stage 2 works best when a Stage 1 video is available.  

Video decoding consumes significant memory. Enable **unload_models** in the **Decoding** nodes to improve speed and prevent out-of-memory errors, even on high-end PCs. On lower-end hardware, you may also need to activate **tiled_vae_decode**.

nodes.title: 💡Info
widgets_values:
Bypassing SageAttention/Triton slightly improves quality but significantly increases generation time!

SageAttention and Trition are not installed in the standard ComfyUI. If you don't know how to install them, it's best to ask an AI. I asked [perplexity.ai](https://perplexity.ai) and was successfully guided through the installation step by step. Since the installation varies depending on the system, universal instructions cannot be provided here. Be sure to create a backup of ComfyUI beforehand, as problems during installation can also cause ComfyUI to stop working.

⚠️‼️If the output video is completely black, this indicates an error with the `sage_attention` model. You should then select the model variant that matches your system configuration. Bypass the group if SageAttention and Triton are not installed‼️⚠️

nodes.title: 💡Video Generation Tips
widgets_values:
The LTX 2.3 model works by first generating a low-resolution video, then upscaling and refining it. With the distilled LoRA, the low-resolution video already has good quality, so generating only this version is a valid workflow for lower-end hardware.

**Upscalers:**  
You can choose between the 1.5x and 2.0x upscalers in the **Load Models** node (last option at the top left). Using 1.5x upscaling delivers better quality in most cases, since the initial video is closer in resolution to the final output, resulting in more detail. The 2.0x option is faster, making it a good choice if your hardware is limited. But if your input image lacks detail, the 2.0x upscaler can outperform the 1.5x upscaler, as it adds more pixels and then reveals finer details.

**Length:**  
LTX 2.3 can generate very long videos. However, going beyond 10 seconds may cause slight desynchronization between video and audio. 

**Resolution:**  
A resolution of about **2.1** megapixels is recommended for the final video, which corresponds to 1080p. A resolution of around 1 megapixel corresponds to approximately 720p video quality.  
Instead of specifying megapixels, you can set the resolution as the size of the shorter side of the video.  
- For the 1.5x upscaler, the value should be divisible by 96.  
- For the 2x upscaler, the value should be divisible by 64.  
If the value doesn't match, the nearest smaller valid number will be used.

**Sampler:**  
- `euler` → more detailed  
- `euler_ancestral` → cleaner  
- `*_cfg_pp` → optimized but much slower and often not noticeably better  or even worse 
 

Using `euler_ancestral` in **Stage 1** and `euler` in **Stage 2** usually gives the most realistic results, as `euler_ancestral` leaves more room for fine details later. But that's not a hard-and-fast rule. `euler` often produces more dynamic results. Just try out what works best for your video.  

**Scheduler:** `linear_quadratic`  

**Steps:** `8–16` (default `8`; higher for less artifacts)  

**Image Input Optimization:**  
If your input image is grainy, you can smooth it by increasing the **start_frame_compression** value (start around 30) in the **Stage 1 Sampler** node. This helps reduce artifacts in the final video. If your input is already clean, no compression is needed.

**Audio Normalization:**  
You can enable **normalize_audio** to improve audio quality. It prevents clipping and boosts quiet sections, making the sound more natural and less tinny. This feature is still experimental and can sometimes worsen the output, as intentional silence may be replaced with inappropriate ambient sound. Therefore, it is generally not recommended.  

**Performance Tips:**  
You can enable the preview, which lets you see what the video will look like in advance. This way, you can stop the process early if you don't like it. But generating the preview slows down the process. Disable it if you want maximum performance.

nodes.title: ℹ️Workflow INFO
widgets_values:
# VideoFlow LTX 2.3 distilled I2V v2.0

## Required Models

### LTX 2.3 Model

You can load the LTX 2.3 model in three formats:

- **Checkpoint**: Video VAE included (extra video VAE file will be ignored).  
- **GGUF**: About twice as slow, but suitable for low VRAM (e.g., 16 GB) when other models are too large.  
- **Diffusion Model**: Video VAE not included.  

#### Notes for the Workflow

- This workflow is designed for the **distilled model**.  
- If you use a non-distilled model, add the **distilled-LoRA** at a strength of **0.6**.  
- Using a distilled model (distilled-LoRA already included) saves memory and generates slightly faster.  
- Tests show image quality is similar with or without extra distilled-LoRA, but **emotions and liveliness** are better without it.  
- The effect of additional LoRAs on a distilled model hasn't been tested; theoretically, it could reduce performance.

If you can't decide which of the available options to download, the recommendations are marked with 👍.

#### Option 1: Checkpoint
Save path 📂`ComfyUI/models/checkpoints`:  

[Download bf16 46.1 GB](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3/resolve/main/ltx-2.3-22b-dev.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-dev.safetensors`  
or  
[Download bf16 distilled 46.1 GB](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3/resolve/main/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled.safetensors`  
or  
[Download fp8 29.1 GB](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3-fp8/resolve/main/ltx-2.3-22b-dev-fp8.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-dev-fp8.safetensors`  
or  
[Download distilled fp8 29.5 GB](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3-fp8/resolve/main/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-fp8.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-fp8.safetensors`👍  

#### Option 2: GGUF
Save path 📂`ComfyUI/models/unet`:  

[Download](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/LTX-2.3-GGUF/tree/main/distilled) Various sizes are available; for 16 GB VRAM, for example, `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-Q4_K_M.gguf`👍 is a good choice   

#### Option 3: Diffusion Model
Save path 📂`ComfyUI/models/diffusion_models`:  

[Download bf16 42 GB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2.3-22b-dev_transformer_only_bf16.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-dev_transformer_only_bf16.saftetensors`  
or  
[Download distilled bf16 42 GB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled_transformer_only_bf16.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled_transformer_only_bf16.safetensors`  
or  
[Download fp8 25 GB only for Nvidia GeForce RTX50xx/40xx](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2-3-22b-dev_transformer_only_fp8_input_scaled.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2-3-22b-dev_transformer_only_fp8_input_scaled.safetensors`  
or  
[Download distilled fp8 25 GB only for Nvidia GeForce RTX50xx/40xx](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled_transformer_only_fp8_input_scaled_v3.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled_transformer_only_fp8_input_scaled_v3.safetensors`👍   
or  
[Download fp8 23.5 GB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2.3-22b-dev_transformer_only_fp8_scaled.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-dev_transformer_only_fp8_scaled.saftetensors`  
or  
[Download distilled fp8 23.5 GB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/diffusion_models/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled_transformer_only_fp8_scaled.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled_transformer_only_fp8_scaled.safetensors`

### Distilled LoRA

The distilled LoRA is only needed if you are not using a distilled model. **Add the LoRA with a `strength` of `0.6`!**  

Save path 📂`ComfyUI/models/loras`:  

[Download 7.61 GB](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3/resolve/main/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-lora-384.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-lora-384.safetensors`  
or  
[Download 2.59 GB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/loras/ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-lora-dynamic_fro09_avg_rank_105_bf16.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-22b-distilled-lora-dynamic_fro09_avg_rank_105_bf16.safetensors`👍    

### Text Encoders

Save path 📂`ComfyUI/models/text_encoders`:  

[Download 2.31 GB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/text_encoders/ltx-2.3_text_projection_bf16.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3_text_projection_bf16.safetensors`  

[Download 24.4 GB](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/ltx-2/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/gemma_3_12B_it.safetensors?download=true) `gemma_3_12B_it.safetensors`  
or  
[Download 9.45 GB](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/ltx-2/resolve/main/split_files/text_encoders/gemma_3_12B_it_fp4_mixed.safetensors?download=true) `gemma_3_12B_it_fp4_mixed.safetensors`👍   

### VAEs

Save path 📂`ComfyUI/models/vae`: 

[Download 365 MB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/vae/LTX23_audio_vae_bf16.safetensors?download=true) `LTX23_audio_vae_bf16.safetensors`  
[Download 1.45 GB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/vae/LTX23_video_vae_bf16.safetensors?download=true) `LTX23_video_vae_bf16.safetensors` (not required when using a checkpoint)  
[Download 23.5 MB](https://huggingface.co/Kijai/LTX2.3_comfy/resolve/main/vae/taeltx2_3.safetensors?download=true) `taeltx2_3.safetensors`  

### Latent Upscale Models

Save path 📂`ComfyUI/models/latent_upscale_models`:  

[Download 1.09 GB](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3/resolve/main/ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x1.5-1.0.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x1.5-1.0.safetensors`  
[Download 996 MB](https://huggingface.co/Lightricks/LTX-2.3/resolve/main/ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x2-1.0.safetensors?download=true) `ltx-2.3-spatial-upscaler-x2-1.0.safetensors`


## Installation

### ComfyUI Manager Installation
[https://github.com/ltdrdata/ComfyUI-Manager?tab=readme-ov-file#comfyui-manager](https://github.com/ltdrdata/ComfyUI-Manager?tab=readme-ov-file#comfyui-manager)

### Installation of Missing Nodes

Missing nodes in this workflow are highlighted in red. To install them, open the ComfyUI Manager and click the 'Install Missing Custom Nodes' button. 

After the installation, restart ComfyUI and refresh the browser page.

## Performance Tips
Make sure you're using the latest graphics card driver. For example, Nvidia released a new version in March 2026 that provided a noticeable performance boost.

You should also keep ComfyUI up to date, not just the nodes. New versions often include performance improvements as well.  

It's only a small improvement, but disabling graphics/hardware acceleration in your browser will free up a bit of VRAM, which can make the difference between slow data swapping and fast VRAM-only usage. Be sure to restart the browser after changing this setting. Keep in mind that this will negatively affect your browser's performance, particularly when watching high-resolution videos. Therefore, this is a temporary improvement intended only for ComfyUI. If you have a video player like VLC open while using ComfyUI, it is recommended to disable hardware acceleration in the Codecs settings as well.

## TL;DR

Check my Civitai profile for updates and other workflows: [https://civitai.com/user/ai839](https://civitai.com/user/ai839)  

I would appreciate a positive review 👍 for this workflow on Civitai.

nodes.title: 💡Final Video Generation Tips
widgets_values:
**Sampler:**  
- `euler` → more detailed, recommended  
- `euler_ancestral` → cleaner  
- `*_cfg_pp` → optimized but much slower and often not noticeably better or even worse 

**Scheduler:** `linear_quadratic`  
**Steps:** `2–8` (default `4`)  
**Denoise:** `0.29` (lower = subtle changes, higher = risk of distortion)

The final video may lose some contrast and show slight lighting fluctuations. You can reduce this by enabling the `color_correction` option in the **Decoding** node. This method transfers the color characteristics of the Stage 1 video to the final video. If you bypass the **Stage 1 Video** group, only the start frame (input image) will be used as the reference. You can enable `start_frame_as_reference` to set the input image as a reference if you want to apply its colors to the entire scene. 

The `reinhard_lab_gpu` method is a good default choice, as it offers a solid balance between performance and quality. Since it also increases contrast, a strength of around `0.7` usually produces a more natural result.

Color correction is computationally expensive and requires a large amount of memory. Reduce the `batch_size` (default `20`) if you run out of memory. It is therefore recommended to first check the video without color correction. If you use fixed seeds in Stage 1 and 2, you can simply enable color_correction afterward and rerun the workflow starting from that step.
